The witnessed over-compaction stands (trim(None) returned Ok and compacted index 7 over six indices of content, with the leader's reads then reporting Trimmed), and the new argument bounds it: both trim paths are bounded by the minimum recorded accepted index, so the bound can only exceed the content of replicas whose recorded value has drifted; a replica whose report is still truthful would lower that minimum, and in the drifted cluster every recorded value is at or above the compacted index, so no in-cluster promise or log sync can fall below it and the underflow that the lead had sourced is not reachable by this route. A fact records that bound property, and the child interpretation keeps conclusion violated with defect_claim asserted for the witnessed over-compaction while moving the hazard from 'untested' to 'argued unreachable in this configuration', with the remainder assigned to any other caller or store that asks below a compacted index.

investigations.discriminator: Whether any producer other than the two trim paths can raise a compacted index past a truthful replica's recorded report in the same configuration (for example a forwarded compaction, a snapshot-driven compaction or a store-level trim), and whether a caller or storage can request a prefix below a compacted index by a route this cluster does not use; the decisive observation would be a compacted index above a truthful replica's content or a panic or silently empty suffix on such a request.

knowledge.statement: Trim's bound is the minimum of the leader's recorded accepted indexes and both trim paths respect it: with no explicit index that minimum is used, and an explicit index above it is refused with that same minimum reported. The bound can therefore exceed only the content of replicas whose recorded accepted index has itself drifted; a replica whose report is still truthful keeps the bound at or below its own content, and no in-cluster promise or log sync can then ask for a prefix below the compacted index.

interpretations.rationale: Witnessed and then narrowed. Receipt ec3329dc273e452aa92bcd44652c116a: with the recorded accepted indexes drifted to 10, 9 and 7 over six indices of content (five entries plus the StopSign) and every node's decided report drifted to 9, the public trim(None) returned no error and compacted index 7 - past the leader's own content - after which the leader's reads of indices 5 and 6 reported Trimmed with a two-element decided-log read (event 14) while the followers still reported accepted 10 and 7 (events 13, 15); the declared comparison requiring the compacted index to reach the six decided indices was violated at the trim event. Narrowing of the consequence, from reading the same derivation: both trim paths are bounded by the minimum recorded accepted index (the explicit-index path refuses any index above it and reports that minimum), so a trim can never compact past the content of a replica whose recorded accepted index is truthful - such a replica would itself supply a lower minimum. That bounds the over-compaction to exceeding the content of replicas whose own recorded values have drifted, which is exactly the witnessed leader, and it also removes the crash path I had sourced from the same lead: a suffix or log-sync request below the compacted index could only come from a replica whose recorded value is below it, and in the drifted cluster every node's recorded value is at or above the compacted index (the trim bound equals the minimum recorded value), so no request in this configuration can reach the arithmetic that would underflow. The hazard therefore stays a sourced possibility for a store or caller that asks below the compacted index by another route, not a consequence of this witness.

counterevidence: Every node's decided report had also drifted to 9, so the documented all-decided precondition was satisfied only in the drifted bookkeeping; the obligation I rely on is that the compacted index must not exceed the entries the leader holds, which it did (7 against 6).
The trim call returned Ok, so nothing in its own result signals the over-compaction; the witness is the compacted index together with the content sampled before and after.

The crash path is now argued unreachable in this configuration rather than merely untested: the trim bound is the minimum recorded accepted index, so every replica's recorded value is at or above the compacted index and no in-cluster suffix request can fall below it.
limitations: The over-compaction is bounded to replicas whose recorded accepted index has drifted; a truthful replica would have kept the bound lower, so the effect cannot silently remove entries a truthful replica has not decided.

The underflow remainder is a property of a storage or caller that requests a prefix below the compacted index by a route other than this cluster's own promises and log syncs; other storage implementations may differ and the trait leaves out-of-range behaviour to the implementer.

The baseline comparisons of the trim receipt are unknown because they were admitted through an event name shared with another case in the same execution; the pre-trim state is asserted from the sampled operands (events 9-11).
One three-node configuration, three reconnection rounds, one leader change and no snapshot creation were exercised; other sizes, producers and entry configurations were not.
